source.primary_manuscript: Codex Vaticanus (B/03; Vatican Library Gr. 1209, 4th c. CE ~325-350)
source.primary_manuscript_contains: Essentially complete New Testament (with some Hebrews + Pauline epistles lacunae); complete Matthew
source.secondary_manuscript: Codex Sinaiticus (א/01; British Library Add. 43725 + Sinai + Leipzig + St. Petersburg fragments, 4th c. CE ~330-360)
source.early_papyri_cross_collation: P64+P67 (Magdalen + Barcelona, late 2nd c. CE ~150-200) preserves Mt 5:20-22, 25-28 — among the earliest substantial witnesses to any portion of Matthew. The P64+P67 readings agree substantially with Vaticanus + Sinaiticus for these verses (Roberts 1953; Skeat 1997; though the date-as-1st-century claim of Thiede has been rejected by the consensus, which dates P64+P67 to late 2nd c. CE).
source.reference_critical_apparatus: NA28 (Nestle-Aland 28th, 2012); UBS5 (United Bible Societies 5th, 2014); SBLGNT (SBL 2010); THGNT (Tyndale House 2017)
source.transliteration_convention: Scholarly Koine Greek transliteration (SBL convention): polytonic-stripped lowercase Latin with diacritics for breathings (h- for rough; nothing for smooth) and Greek-specific letters (ē for eta, ō for omega, ph for phi, ch for chi, ps for psi, th for theta, rh for rho with rough breathing); ai/ei/oi/au/eu/ou diphthongs preserved; accent marks generally omitted in scholarly translit
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against Vaticanus + Sinaiticus + P64+P67 original codicology + the NA28/UBS5/SBLGNT critical apparatus
source.fetchedFrom: SBLGNT public-domain edition (Holmes 2010) + NA28 reference (where variants are documented) + P64+P67 readings per Skeat 1997
source.citation: Aland, Aland, Karavidopoulos, Martini, Metzger, eds., *Novum Testamentum Graece*, 28th ed. (Nestle-Aland, Stuttgart 2012). UBS5 = Aland et al., *The Greek New Testament*, 5th ed. (United Bible Societies 2014). Holmes, M. W., ed., *The Greek New Testament: SBL Edition* (SBL 2010; public-domain). Jongkind, D., ed., *The Greek New Testament*, Tyndale House (Crossway 2017). Codex Vaticanus: Vatican Library Gr. 1209 (4th c. CE). Codex Sinaiticus: British Library Add. 43725 + Sinai + Leipzig + St. Petersburg fragments (4th c. CE). P64+P67 = Magdalen + Barcelona (late 2nd c. CE); Skeat, T. C., 'The Oldest Manuscript of the Four Gospels?' (NTS 43, 1997, 1-34). Davies-Allison ICC 1988-1997; Luz Hermeneia 2001-2007 (Mt 1-7 vol); France NICNT 2007; Hagner WBC 1993-1995; Nolland NIGTC 2005; Betz, H. D., *The Sermon on the Mount* (Hermeneia 1995); Levine-Brettler JANT 2017.
source.paleography_note: The Koine Greek text is preserved in polytonic form as transmitted via SBLGNT. The P64+P67 cross-collation for vv.20-22, 25-28 confirms the consensus reading. The early Greek manuscripts use scriptio continua; the SBLGNT polytonic-with-spaces is the modern critical reconstruction. Nomina sacra (ΙΣ ΧΣ ΚΣ ΘΣ ΠΝΑ ΥΣ ΠΗΡ ΟΥΝΟΣ for οὐρανός) appear abbreviated in the uncials.

verses.text: Ἰδὼν δὲ τοὺς ὄχλους ἀνέβη εἰς τὸ ὄρος· καὶ καθίσαντος αὐτοῦ προσῆλθαν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ·
verses.translit: Idōn de tous ochlous anebē eis to oros· kai kathisantos autou prosēlthan autō hoi mathētai autou·
verses.notes: MAJOR FRAMING — the Sermon-on-the-Mount opening. *to oros* (the mountain) deliberately echoes Sinai (Exod 19; cf. Matthew's broader Moses-typology: 5 great discourses paralleling 5 books of Torah; cf. Davies-Allison ICC 1.423-427; Allison, *The New Moses* 1993). The teaching-seated posture (*kathisantos*) is the rabbinic authoritative-teaching posture (cf. Mt 23:2 'the seat of Moses'). Variant: Sinaiticus reads *prosēlthon* (came to him); Vaticanus reads *prosēlthan* (Hellenistic 1st aorist ending). Cross-corpus: cf. Luke 6:17-49 'sermon on the plain' parallel.

verses.text: καὶ ἀνοίξας τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ ἐδίδασκεν αὐτοὺς λέγων·
verses.translit: kai anoixas to stoma autou edidasken autous legōn·
verses.notes: The formulaic 'opened his mouth' (LXX-idiom, cf. Job 3:1; Ps 78:2 LXX) marks solemn discourse. Davies-Allison ICC 1.427-428.

verses.text: Μακάριοι οἱ πτωχοὶ τῷ πνεύματι, ὅτι αὐτῶν ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν.
verses.translit: Makarioi hoi ptōchoi tō pneumati, hoti autōn estin hē basileia tōn ouranōn.
verses.notes: BEATITUDE 1 — *makarioi hoi ptōchoi tō pneumati* ("blessed are the poor in spirit"). The Lukan parallel (Luke 6:20) lacks *tō pneumati* and reads simply 'blessed are the poor' — the Matthean spiritualization is widely seen as redactional. The Hebrew background (ʿănāwîm — the pious poor; cf. Ps 37; Isa 61:1; 1QM 14:7 from Qumran) frames the materially-poor as the eschatologically-favored. *basileia tōn ouranōn* (kingdom of the heavens) is the Matthean variant of the otherwise standard *basileia tou theou* — likely a Jewish-pious circumlocution avoiding the divine name. **RAËLIAN CANON CITATION SITE**: the Beatitudes (vv. 3-12) are engaged in *The Role of Christ* as 'the ethical foundation taught by the Elohim messenger.' Davies-Allison ICC 1.442-449; Betz Hermeneia 1995 109-118.

verses.text: μακάριοι οἱ πενθοῦντες, ὅτι αὐτοὶ παρακληθήσονται.
verses.translit: makarioi hoi penthountes, hoti autoi paraklēthēsontai.
verses.notes: BEATITUDE 2 — the mourners. *paraklēthēsontai* (will be comforted) — divine passive (action attributed to God without naming the agent). Direct allusion to Isa 61:2-3 LXX *parakalesai pantas tous penthountas* (to comfort all who mourn). Some MSS (including Sinaiticus's order) place this verse after v.5 (the meek-Beatitude); the order varies in the early witnesses. Davies-Allison ICC 1.447-449.

verses.text: μακάριοι οἱ πραεῖς, ὅτι αὐτοὶ κληρονομήσουσιν τὴν γῆν.
verses.translit: makarioi hoi praeis, hoti autoi klēronomēsousin tēn gēn.
verses.notes: BEATITUDE 3 — the meek. Direct citation of Ps 37:11 LXX (*hoi de praeis klēronomēsousin gēn*). *praus* = gentle / meek / non-violent — in Hellenistic ethics also a Stoic virtue (cf. Aristotle EN 4.5; Epictetus); in Jewish background, the *ʿănāw* of the Psalmist. *klēronomēsousin tēn gēn* — eschatological land-inheritance. Davies-Allison ICC 1.449-451.

verses.text: μακάριοι οἱ πεινῶντες καὶ διψῶντες τὴν δικαιοσύνην, ὅτι αὐτοὶ χορτασθήσονται.
verses.translit: makarioi hoi peinōntes kai dipsōntes tēn dikaiosynēn, hoti autoi chortasthēsontai.
verses.notes: BEATITUDE 4 — hungering and thirsting for righteousness. *dikaiosynē* is a major Matthean theme (cf. 5:10, 5:20, 6:1, 6:33) — denoting both ethical-conduct righteousness and God's vindicating-righteousness. *chortasthēsontai* (will be fed) — divine passive.

verses.text: μακάριοι οἱ ἐλεήμονες, ὅτι αὐτοὶ ἐλεηθήσονται.
verses.translit: makarioi hoi eleēmones, hoti autoi eleēthēsontai.
verses.notes: BEATITUDE 5 — the merciful. The *lex talionis* of grace structure (mercy → mercy) — cf. Mt 6:14-15, 18:21-35. Cross-corpus: cf. m. Avot 5:7 (rabbinic measure-for-measure principle); cf. Sir 28:1-7.

verses.text: μακάριοι οἱ καθαροὶ τῇ καρδίᾳ, ὅτι αὐτοὶ τὸν θεὸν ὄψονται.
verses.translit: makarioi hoi katharoi tē kardia, hoti autoi ton theon opsontai.
verses.notes: BEATITUDE 6 — pure in heart. Direct allusion to Ps 24:3-4 LXX (*tis anabēsetai eis to oros tou kyriou ... athōos chersin kai katharos tē kardia*). *ton theon opsontai* (will see God) — the visio-Dei promise; cf. 1 Cor 13:12; 1 John 3:2; Heb 12:14. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: 'will see God' should NOT be pre-resolved into a literal Elohim-physical-presence reading (Raëlian canon) NOR into a beatific-vision mystical-theology reading; preserve as eschatological theophany.

verses.text: μακάριοι οἱ εἰρηνοποιοί, ὅτι αὐτοὶ υἱοὶ θεοῦ κληθήσονται.
verses.translit: makarioi hoi eirēnopoioi, hoti autoi huioi theou klēthēsontai.
verses.notes: BEATITUDE 7 — the peacemakers. *eirēnopoios* is rare in classical Greek (occurring in Plutarch, Philo); in Greco-Roman political vocabulary the title was sometimes applied to emperors (Augustus as *eirēnopoios*). *huioi theou* — sons of God; eschatological adoption (cf. Rom 8:14-17; Hos 1:10).

verses.text: μακάριοι οἱ δεδιωγμένοι ἕνεκεν δικαιοσύνης, ὅτι αὐτῶν ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν.
verses.translit: makarioi hoi dediōgmenoi heneken dikaiosynēs, hoti autōn estin hē basileia tōn ouranōn.
verses.notes: BEATITUDE 8 — the persecuted-for-righteousness. Structural inclusio with Beatitude 1 (v.3) — both end *autōn estin hē basileia tōn ouranōn*, framing the eight as a unit. The pluperfect-passive participle *dediōgmenoi* (have-been-persecuted) suggests an audience already experiencing persecution — locating the Matthean community in a setting of Jewish-Christian post-70-CE tension.

verses.text: μακάριοί ἐστε ὅταν ὀνειδίσωσιν ὑμᾶς καὶ διώξωσιν καὶ εἴπωσιν πᾶν πονηρὸν καθ' ὑμῶν ψευδόμενοι ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ·
verses.translit: makarioi este hotan oneidisōsin hymas kai diōxōsin kai eipōsin pan ponēron kath' hymōn pseudomenoi heneken emou·
verses.notes: BEATITUDE 9 — direct-address expansion of v.10. Shift from third-person *makarioi hoi* to second-person *makarioi este*. Variant: some witnesses (Vaticanus among them) omit *pseudomenoi* (lying); SBLGNT/NA28 include it. The *heneken emou* (for my sake) makes the Christological reference explicit — the persecution is incurred *because of* the speaker.

verses.text: χαίρετε καὶ ἀγαλλιᾶσθε, ὅτι ὁ μισθὸς ὑμῶν πολὺς ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς· οὕτως γὰρ ἐδίωξαν τοὺς προφήτας τοὺς πρὸ ὑμῶν.
verses.translit: chairete kai agalliasthe, hoti ho misthos hymōn polys en tois ouranois· houtōs gar ediōxan tous prophētas tous pro hymōn.
verses.notes: The reward-in-heaven motif. The persecuted-prophet typology (cf. 2 Chr 36:15-16; Neh 9:26; Mt 23:29-37; Acts 7:52) frames the disciples as continuing the prophetic-suffering line.

verses.text: Ὑμεῖς ἐστε τὸ ἅλας τῆς γῆς· ἐὰν δὲ τὸ ἅλας μωρανθῇ, ἐν τίνι ἁλισθήσεται; εἰς οὐδὲν ἰσχύει ἔτι εἰ μὴ βληθὲν ἔξω καταπατεῖσθαι ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων.
verses.translit: Hymeis este to halas tēs gēs· ean de to halas mōranthē, en tini halisthēsetai? eis ouden ischyei eti ei mē blēthen exō katapateisthai hypo tōn anthrōpōn.
verses.notes: SALT METAPHOR. *mōranthē* literally = 'become foolish' (cognate to *mōros* fool) — the Greek pun on tasteless-salt = foolish-salt is striking. Cross-corpus: cf. Mark 9:49-50; Luke 14:34-35; Col 4:6 ('let your speech be seasoned with salt'). The Dead-Sea / Sodom salt-deposits-with-impurity background may be relevant.

verses.text: Ὑμεῖς ἐστε τὸ φῶς τοῦ κόσμου. οὐ δύναται πόλις κρυβῆναι ἐπάνω ὄρους κειμένη·
verses.translit: Hymeis este to phōs tou kosmou. ou dynatai polis krybēnai epanō orous keimenē·
verses.notes: LIGHT METAPHOR. The *polis epi orous* (city on a mountain) image — possibly Jerusalem (Isa 2:2-3; Mic 4:1-2), possibly Sepphoris (visible from Nazareth). *to phōs tou kosmou* — Jesus uses the same self-designation at John 8:12. The Israel-as-light-to-nations motif (Isa 42:6, 49:6, 60:3) is now applied to the disciples.

verses.text: οὐδὲ καίουσιν λύχνον καὶ τιθέασιν αὐτὸν ὑπὸ τὸν μόδιον ἀλλ' ἐπὶ τὴν λυχνίαν, καὶ λάμπει πᾶσιν τοῖς ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ.
verses.translit: oude kaiousin lychnon kai titheasin auton hypo ton modion all' epi tēn lychnian, kai lampei pasin tois en tē oikia.
verses.notes: LAMP UNDER A BASKET — *modion* (a Latin loanword: *modius* = a dry-measure container holding ~9 liters). cf. Mark 4:21; Luke 8:16, 11:33. The standard Galilean peasant house had a single oil lamp on a lamp-stand illuminating the single common room.

verses.text: οὕτως λαμψάτω τὸ φῶς ὑμῶν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ὅπως ἴδωσιν ὑμῶν τὰ καλὰ ἔργα καὶ δοξάσωσιν τὸν πατέρα ὑμῶν τὸν ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.
verses.translit: houtōs lampsatō to phōs hymōn emprosthen tōn anthrōpōn, hopōs idōsin hymōn ta kala erga kai doxasōsin ton patera hymōn ton en tois ouranois.
verses.notes: First Matthean occurrence of *patēr hymōn ho en tois ouranois* ("your Father in the heavens") — the distinctive Matthean address-form for God. The phrase recurs throughout the Sermon (5:45, 5:48, 6:1, 6:9, 7:11, etc.) and is central to the Lord's-Prayer opening at 6:9. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: the Raëlian-canon reads *patēr en tois ouranois* literally as 'Father in the heavens / among the stars' = Elohim. Preserve text; do not pre-resolve.

verses.text: Μὴ νομίσητε ὅτι ἦλθον καταλῦσαι τὸν νόμον ἢ τοὺς προφήτας· οὐκ ἦλθον καταλῦσαι ἀλλὰ πληρῶσαι·
verses.translit: Mē nomisēte hoti ēlthon katalysai ton nomon ē tous prophētas· ouk ēlthon katalysai alla plērōsai·
verses.notes: MAJOR FRAMING — the law-fulfillment programmatic statement. **RAËLIAN CANON CITATION SITE**: Raël *The Role of Christ* engages this as 'the continuity of Elohim revelation.' **HIGH LENS-RISK FOR SUPERSESSIONISM**: this verse has been historically misused to support Christian-supersessionist readings (Christ-abolishes-Torah). The Matthean text states the opposite: *ouk ēlthon katalysai* (I came NOT to abolish). *plērōsai* (to fulfill) can mean (a) to bring to its intended completion / interpretive realization, (b) to embody / live out fully, (c) to fulfill prophetic predictions. Davies-Allison ICC 1.481-487; Luz Hermeneia 1.261-271; Levine-Brettler JANT ad loc. **EDITOR DISAVOW supersessionism explicitly.**

verses.text: ἀμὴν γὰρ λέγω ὑμῖν, ἕως ἂν παρέλθῃ ὁ οὐρανὸς καὶ ἡ γῆ, ἰῶτα ἓν ἢ μία κεραία οὐ μὴ παρέλθῃ ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου, ἕως ἂν πάντα γένηται.
verses.translit: amēn gar legō hymin, heōs an parelthē ho ouranos kai hē gē, iōta hen ē mia keraia ou mē parelthē apo tou nomou, heōs an panta genētai.
verses.notes: TORAH-PERMANENCE STATEMENT. *iōta* (the smallest Greek letter, ι; cf. Hebrew yod י the smallest Hebrew letter); *keraia* (lit. 'little horn' — a decorative tag/serif distinguishing similar Hebrew letters: ב/כ, ד/ר, ה/ח). Together they express 'not the smallest mark.' Parallel: Luke 16:17. The double *heōs an* construction has been the locus of major dispute: does the Torah remain binding only until *panta genētai* ("all has come to pass") = until eschatological completion = forever-effectively, or until a different fulfillment point? cf. Davies-Allison ICC 1.490-495. **RAËLIAN CANON ENGAGES** as 'continuity of revelation' — preserve, do not theologize.

verses.text: ὃς ἐὰν οὖν λύσῃ μίαν τῶν ἐντολῶν τούτων τῶν ἐλαχίστων καὶ διδάξῃ οὕτως τοὺς ἀνθρώπους, ἐλάχιστος κληθήσεται ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν· ὃς δ' ἂν ποιήσῃ καὶ διδάξῃ, οὗτος μέγας κληθήσεται ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν.
verses.translit: hos ean oun lysē mian tōn entolōn toutōn tōn elachistōn kai didaxē houtōs tous anthrōpous, elachistos klēthēsetai en tē basileia tōn ouranōn· hos d' an poiēsē kai didaxē, houtos megas klēthēsetai en tē basileia tōn ouranōn.
verses.notes: *tōn elachistōn* (the least of the commandments) reflects the rabbinic distinction between 'light' and 'weighty' commandments (cf. m. Avot 2:1; 4:2). The verse states that even the least Torah-commandment retains validity for kingdom-status. Strongly anti-supersessionist. Davies-Allison ICC 1.495-498.

verses.text: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐὰν μὴ περισσεύσῃ ὑμῶν ἡ δικαιοσύνη πλεῖον τῶν γραμματέων καὶ Φαρισαίων, οὐ μὴ εἰσέλθητε εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν.
verses.translit: legō gar hymin hoti ean mē perisseusē hymōn hē dikaiosynē pleion tōn grammateōn kai Pharisaiōn, ou mē eiselthēte eis tēn basileian tōn ouranōn.
verses.notes: PAPYRUS-CROSS-COLLATED VERSE — preserved in P64+P67 (Magdalen, late 2nd c. CE); the P64+P67 reading agrees with Vaticanus + Sinaiticus. *perisseusē* (exceed/surpass) — the call is not to less Torah-observance but to MORE — refining/intensifying the legal interpretation. **EDITOR FLAG**: do NOT translate as 'unless your righteousness be MORE LEGALISTIC than the Pharisees' — the Matthean meaning is qualitative intensification of intent, not quantitative addition of rules. Davies-Allison ICC 1.499-503.

verses.text: Ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη τοῖς ἀρχαίοις· Οὐ φονεύσεις· ὃς δ' ἂν φονεύσῃ, ἔνοχος ἔσται τῇ κρίσει.
verses.translit: Ēkousate hoti errethē tois archaiois· Ou phoneuseis· hos d' an phoneusē, enochos estai tē krisei.
verses.notes: FIRST ANTITHESIS — murder. *Ēkousate hoti errethē* ("you have heard that it was said") opens the six-fold antithesis sequence (vv.21-22, 27-28, 31-32, 33-34, 38-39, 43-44). Direct citation of Exod 20:13 / Deut 5:17 LXX (*ou phoneuseis*). The 'said to those of ancient times' frame distances the speaker from the giving-of-Torah event without abolishing the commandment (cf. v.17). PAPYRUS-CROSS-COLLATED — P64+P67 preserves v.22.

verses.text: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶς ὁ ὀργιζόμενος τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ ἔνοχος ἔσται τῇ κρίσει· ὃς δ' ἂν εἴπῃ τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ· Ῥακά, ἔνοχος ἔσται τῷ συνεδρίῳ· ὃς δ' ἂν εἴπῃ· Μωρέ, ἔνοχος ἔσται εἰς τὴν γέενναν τοῦ πυρός.
verses.translit: egō de legō hymin hoti pas ho orgizomenos tō adelphō autou enochos estai tē krisei· hos d' an eipē tō adelphō autou· Rhaka, enochos estai tō synedriō· hos d' an eipē· Mōre, enochos estai eis tēn geennan tou puros.
verses.notes: PAPYRUS-CROSS-COLLATED — P64+P67 preserves this verse. **TEXTUAL VARIANT — KEY**: many late witnesses add *eikē* (without cause) after *adelphō autou* — softening the absolute prohibition. The earliest witnesses (Vaticanus, Sinaiticus, P64+P67) omit *eikē*; NA28/SBLGNT/THGNT all read without *eikē*. The longer reading is a scribal-conscience harmonization. *Rhaka* — an Aramaic loanword (rēqā = 'empty one' = idiot/blockhead). *Mōre* — Greek 'fool' (cognate to *mōros*). *geenna* — Aramaized Hebrew *gê-Hinnōm* (Valley of Hinnom outside Jerusalem) — the post-biblical eschatological-punishment toponym. Davies-Allison ICC 1.511-516.

verses.text: ἐὰν οὖν προσφέρῃς τὸ δῶρόν σου ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον κἀκεῖ μνησθῇς ὅτι ὁ ἀδελφός σου ἔχει τι κατὰ σοῦ,
verses.translit: ean oun prospherēs to dōron sou epi to thysiastērion kakei mnēsthēs hoti ho adelphos sou echei ti kata sou,
verses.notes: Reconciliation-before-Temple-offering. The verse pre-supposes a functioning Temple cult — locating the Matthean tradition (or at least this teaching) in a pre-70-CE setting (or, as Matthean redaction post-70, preserving the pre-70 teaching). cf. m. Yoma 8:9 (sins between humans not atoned by Yom Kippur until reconciliation made).

verses.text: ἄφες ἐκεῖ τὸ δῶρόν σου ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου καὶ ὕπαγε πρῶτον διαλλάγηθι τῷ ἀδελφῷ σου, καὶ τότε ἐλθὼν πρόσφερε τὸ δῶρόν σου.
verses.translit: aphes ekei to dōron sou emprosthen tou thysiastēriou kai hypage prōton diallagēthi tō adelphō sou, kai tote elthōn prosphere to dōron sou.
verses.notes: *diallagēthi* (be reconciled) — passive imperative; the initiative for reconciliation lies with the one bringing the offering, regardless of who was at fault. Continues the reconciliation-priority-over-cult theme of v.23.

verses.text: ἴσθι εὐνοῶν τῷ ἀντιδίκῳ σου ταχὺ ἕως ὅτου εἶ μετ' αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ, μήποτέ σε παραδῷ ὁ ἀντίδικος τῷ κριτῇ, καὶ ὁ κριτὴς τῷ ὑπηρέτῃ, καὶ εἰς φυλακὴν βληθήσῃ·
verses.translit: isthi eunoōn tō antidikō sou tachy heōs hotou ei met' autou en tē hodō, mēpote se paradō ho antidikos tō kritē, kai ho kritēs tō hypēretē, kai eis phylakēn blēthēsē·
verses.notes: PAPYRUS-CROSS-COLLATED — P64+P67 preserves this verse. Settle-out-of-court parable (Luke 12:58-59 parallel). The Roman legal context of *antidikos* (legal adversary) → *kritēs* (judge) → *hypēretēs* (court-officer) → *phylakē* (prison) shows the standard 1st-c. judicial sequence.

verses.text: ἀμὴν λέγω σοι, οὐ μὴ ἐξέλθῃς ἐκεῖθεν ἕως ἂν ἀποδῷς τὸν ἔσχατον κοδράντην.
verses.translit: amēn legō soi, ou mē exelthēs ekeithen heōs an apodōs ton eschaton kodrantēn.
verses.notes: PAPYRUS-CROSS-COLLATED — P64+P67 preserves this verse. *kodrantēs* — Latin loanword (*quadrans* — the smallest Roman copper coin, 1/4 of an *as*). The Roman-monetary-system reference firmly anchors the Matthean tradition in a Roman-administered setting.

verses.text: Ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη· Οὐ μοιχεύσεις.
verses.translit: Ēkousate hoti errethē· Ou moicheuseis.
verses.notes: PAPYRUS-CROSS-COLLATED — P64+P67 preserves this verse. SECOND ANTITHESIS — adultery. Direct citation of Exod 20:14 / Deut 5:18 LXX. Variant: some witnesses add *tois archaiois* ("to those of ancient times") harmonizing with v.21; NA28/SBLGNT/THGNT omit, following Vaticanus + Sinaiticus + P64+P67.

verses.text: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶς ὁ βλέπων γυναῖκα πρὸς τὸ ἐπιθυμῆσαι αὐτὴν ἤδη ἐμοίχευσεν αὐτὴν ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: egō de legō hymin hoti pas ho blepōn gynaika pros to epithymēsai autēn ēdē emoicheusen autēn en tē kardia autou.
verses.notes: PAPYRUS-CROSS-COLLATED — P64+P67 preserves this verse, agreeing substantially with Vaticanus + Sinaiticus. The interiorization of adultery (intention = act). *epithymēsai* (to desire) echoes the LXX Decalogue *ouk epithymēseis* (Exod 20:17; Deut 5:21) — the antithesis links the prohibition of adultery (7th commandment) to the prohibition of coveting (10th). Cross-corpus: cf. Job 31:1; cf. b. Berakhot 24a (rabbinic gaze-discipline).

verses.text: εἰ δὲ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου ὁ δεξιὸς σκανδαλίζει σε, ἔξελε αὐτὸν καὶ βάλε ἀπὸ σοῦ, συμφέρει γάρ σοι ἵνα ἀπόληται ἓν τῶν μελῶν σου καὶ μὴ ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου βληθῇ εἰς γέενναν.
verses.translit: ei de ho ophthalmos sou ho dexios skandalizei se, exele auton kai bale apo sou, sympherei gar soi hina apolētai hen tōn melōn sou kai mē holon to sōma sou blēthē eis geennan.
verses.notes: HYPERBOLIC EYE-PLUCKING. The hyperbole functions as a Semitic rhetorical intensifier — not a literal-amputation prescription. cf. Davies-Allison ICC 1.523-525. The *ophthalmos ... dexios* (right eye) singled out as the more important / valuable; cf. 1 Sam 11:2 (Nahash threatening right-eye gouging). Parallel: Mt 18:9; Mark 9:47.

verses.text: καὶ εἰ ἡ δεξιά σου χεὶρ σκανδαλίζει σε, ἔκκοψον αὐτὴν καὶ βάλε ἀπὸ σοῦ, συμφέρει γάρ σοι ἵνα ἀπόληται ἓν τῶν μελῶν σου καὶ μὴ ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου εἰς γέενναν ἀπέλθῃ.
verses.translit: kai ei hē dexia sou cheir skandalizei se, ekkopson autēn kai bale apo sou, sympherei gar soi hina apolētai hen tōn melōn sou kai mē holon to sōma sou eis geennan apelthē.
verses.notes: Parallel hyperbole — right hand. The *dexia* (right) intensifier matches v.29. Variant: Sinaiticus omits this verse (whole-verse omission) — likely scribal homoioteleuton (eye-skip between v.29 *eis geennan* and v.30 *eis geennan*). NA28/SBLGNT/Vaticanus include.

verses.text: Ἐρρέθη δέ· Ὃς ἂν ἀπολύσῃ τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ, δότω αὐτῇ ἀποστάσιον.
verses.translit: Errethē de· Hos an apolysē tēn gynaika autou, dotō autē apostasion.
verses.notes: THIRD ANTITHESIS — divorce. Citation of Deut 24:1 LXX (the divorce-certificate provision). *apostasion* = certificate of divorce (legal document). The thesis statement here is brief; the antithesis expansion follows in v.32.

verses.text: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶς ὁ ἀπολύων τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ παρεκτὸς λόγου πορνείας ποιεῖ αὐτὴν μοιχευθῆναι, καὶ ὃς ἐὰν ἀπολελυμένην γαμήσῃ μοιχᾶται.
verses.translit: egō de legō hymin hoti pas ho apolyōn tēn gynaika autou parektos logou porneias poiei autēn moicheuthēnai, kai hos ean apolelymenēn gamēsē moichatai.
verses.notes: MATTHEAN EXCEPTION-CLAUSE. *parektos logou porneias* ("except for a matter of porneia") — the famous Matthean exception (also at 19:9) absent from the Markan (Mk 10:11-12) and Lukan (Lk 16:18) and Pauline (1 Cor 7:10-11) parallel traditions. *porneia* — ambiguous: sexual immorality / unchastity / illicit unions. Davies-Allison ICC 1.528-532 (extensive discussion). The exception has been the locus of every subsequent Christian divorce-theology debate; the Catholic 'no-divorce' position reads *porneia* as referring only to invalid unions (incest), Protestant traditions read it as referring to adultery.

verses.text: Πάλιν ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη τοῖς ἀρχαίοις· Οὐκ ἐπιορκήσεις, ἀποδώσεις δὲ τῷ κυρίῳ τοὺς ὅρκους σου.
verses.translit: Palin ēkousate hoti errethē tois archaiois· Ouk epiorkēseis, apodōseis de tō kyriō tous horkous sou.
verses.notes: FOURTH ANTITHESIS — oaths. Composite citation: Lev 19:12 (*ouk omeisthe tō onomati mou ep' adikō*) + Num 30:2 / Deut 23:21-23 (the oath-fulfillment provisions). *epiorkein* = to swear falsely / perjure.

verses.text: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν μὴ ὀμόσαι ὅλως· μήτε ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, ὅτι θρόνος ἐστὶν τοῦ θεοῦ·
verses.translit: egō de legō hymin mē omosai holōs· mēte en tō ouranō, hoti thronos estin tou theou·
verses.notes: ABSOLUTE OATH-PROHIBITION. *mē omosai holōs* (do not swear at all) — cf. Jas 5:12 (the only other NT passage with the same absolute formulation, often considered an independent witness to the Jesus-tradition). The Essene parallel (Josephus *BJ* 2.135; CD 15:1-5; 1QS 5:8) shows a similar oath-prohibition tradition in 1st-c. Judaism. *thronos tou theou* — heaven-as-throne (Isa 66:1).

verses.text: μήτε ἐν τῇ γῇ, ὅτι ὑποπόδιόν ἐστιν τῶν ποδῶν αὐτοῦ· μήτε εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, ὅτι πόλις ἐστὶν τοῦ μεγάλου βασιλέως·
verses.translit: mēte en tē gē, hoti hypopodion estin tōn podōn autou· mēte eis Hierosolyma, hoti polis estin tou megalou basileōs·
verses.notes: Continuing the oath-prohibition catalog. Earth = footstool (Isa 66:1); Jerusalem = city of the great king (Ps 48:2 LXX). Each oath-formula is shown to invoke God indirectly, hence to fall under the same prohibition.

verses.text: μήτε ἐν τῇ κεφαλῇ σου ὀμόσῃς, ὅτι οὐ δύνασαι μίαν τρίχα λευκὴν ποιῆσαι ἢ μέλαιναν.
verses.translit: mēte en tē kephalē sou omosēs, hoti ou dynasai mian tricha leukēn poiēsai ē melainan.
verses.notes: The head-oath. Lack of control over hair color (*leukēn ē melainan*) = humanity's lack of authority to bind one's destiny by oath. Cross-corpus: cf. Mt 6:27 (cannot add one cubit to lifespan).

verses.text: ἔστω δὲ ὁ λόγος ὑμῶν ναὶ ναί, οὒ οὔ· τὸ δὲ περισσὸν τούτων ἐκ τοῦ πονηροῦ ἐστιν.
verses.translit: estō de ho logos hymōn nai nai, ou ou· to de perisson toutōn ek tou ponērou estin.
verses.notes: *nai nai, ou ou* — the simple-truth-affirmation formula. *ek tou ponērou* — ambiguous: either 'from the evil one' (genitive of *ho ponēros* = Satan; the substantive masculine reading) or 'from evil' (neuter abstract). Both readings have ancient defenders. cf. Jas 5:12 parallel.

verses.text: Ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη· Ὀφθαλμὸν ἀντὶ ὀφθαλμοῦ καὶ ὀδόντα ἀντὶ ὀδόντος.
verses.translit: Ēkousate hoti errethē· Ophthalmon anti ophthalmou kai odonta anti odontos.
verses.notes: FIFTH ANTITHESIS — *lex talionis*. Direct citation of Exod 21:24 / Lev 24:20 / Deut 19:21 LXX. The HB *lex talionis* is itself a *limitation* of vengeance (one eye max, not escalating retribution); the antithesis goes further to remove retaliation entirely.

verses.text: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν μὴ ἀντιστῆναι τῷ πονηρῷ· ἀλλ' ὅστις σε ῥαπίζει εἰς τὴν δεξιὰν σιαγόνα, στρέψον αὐτῷ καὶ τὴν ἄλλην·
verses.translit: egō de legō hymin mē antistēnai tō ponērō· all' hostis se rhapizei eis tēn dexian siagona, strepson autō kai tēn allēn·
verses.notes: NON-RESISTANCE / TURN-THE-OTHER-CHEEK. *mē antistēnai tō ponērō* — 'do not resist the evil(doer)' or 'do not resist evil(by-evil-means).' *tēn dexian siagona* (right cheek) — striking the right cheek with the right hand requires a backhanded blow (= an insult-strike, not a violence-strike); the gesture-grammar of Greco-Roman honor culture is at play. cf. Wink, *Engaging the Powers* 1992 (the 'third-way' nonviolent-resistance reading). Cross-corpus: cf. Lam 3:30 LXX; cf. Stoic non-retaliation ethics (Marcus Aurelius).

verses.text: καὶ τῷ θέλοντί σοι κριθῆναι καὶ τὸν χιτῶνά σου λαβεῖν, ἄφες αὐτῷ καὶ τὸ ἱμάτιον·
verses.translit: kai tō thelonti soi krithēnai kai ton chitōna sou labein, aphes autō kai to himation·
verses.notes: The tunic-cloak escalation. *chitōn* (inner tunic) vs *himation* (outer cloak/garment) — the *himation* was legally non-takable as security (Exod 22:25-26; Deut 24:12-13) since it served as the poor man's blanket. Giving up even the legally-protected outer cloak intensifies the non-retaliation.

verses.text: καὶ ὅστις σε ἀγγαρεύσει μίλιον ἕν, ὕπαγε μετ' αὐτοῦ δύο.
verses.translit: kai hostis se angareusei milion hen, hypage met' autou dyo.
verses.notes: GO-THE-SECOND-MILE. *angareusei* — Persian loanword (cognate to modern French *angarie*) referring to the imperial requisition-system whereby Roman soldiers could compel a civilian to carry baggage for one *milion* (Roman mile, ~1.48 km). cf. Mt 27:32 (Simon of Cyrene *ēngareusan*). The verse pre-supposes the Roman-occupation context.

verses.text: τῷ αἰτοῦντί σε δός, καὶ τὸν θέλοντα ἀπὸ σοῦ δανίσασθαι μὴ ἀποστραφῇς.
verses.translit: tō aitounti se dos, kai ton thelonta apo sou danisasthai mē apostraphēs.
verses.notes: Generous-giving / interest-free-lending injunction. The Torah's interest-free-loan provisions to fellow Israelites (Exod 22:25; Lev 25:35-37; Deut 23:19-20) are intensified here to universal generosity. Cross-corpus: cf. Sir 4:1-6; cf. Tob 4:7-11.

verses.text: Ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη· Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου καὶ μισήσεις τὸν ἐχθρόν σου.
verses.translit: Ēkousate hoti errethē· Agapēseis ton plēsion sou kai misēseis ton echthron sou.
verses.notes: SIXTH ANTITHESIS — love-of-neighbor. Citation of Lev 19:18 (*agapēseis ton plēsion sou*) — but the *kai misēseis ton echthron sou* (and hate your enemy) is NOT in the Hebrew Bible. Possible sources: the Qumran *Community Rule* 1QS 1:9-11 (love sons of light, hate sons of darkness); or popular Galilean Torah-paraphrase. The 'thesis' here is being treated as a popular interpretation, not as direct Torah-citation. Davies-Allison ICC 1.549-553.

verses.text: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἐχθροὺς ὑμῶν καὶ προσεύχεσθε ὑπὲρ τῶν διωκόντων ὑμᾶς·
verses.translit: egō de legō hymin, agapate tous echthrous hymōn kai proseuchesthe hyper tōn diōkontōn hymas·
verses.notes: ENEMY-LOVE COMMAND. Variant: many later (Byzantine) witnesses expand: *agapate tous echthrous hymōn, eulogeite tous katarōmenous hymas, kalōs poieite tois misousin hymas, kai proseuchesthe hyper tōn epēreazontōn hymas kai diōkontōn hymas* — a four-fold expansion harmonizing with Luke 6:27-28. The earliest witnesses (Vaticanus, Sinaiticus, P64+P67 [partial]) preserve the shorter Matthean form. NA28/SBLGNT/THGNT all read the shorter form. Cross-corpus: cf. Prov 25:21 (kindness to enemies); Rom 12:14-21; cf. Stoic *philanthrōpia* (Seneca *De ira*).

verses.text: ὅπως γένησθε υἱοὶ τοῦ πατρὸς ὑμῶν τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς, ὅτι τὸν ἥλιον αὐτοῦ ἀνατέλλει ἐπὶ πονηροὺς καὶ ἀγαθοὺς καὶ βρέχει ἐπὶ δικαίους καὶ ἀδίκους.
verses.translit: hopōs genēsthe huioi tou patros hymōn tou en ouranois, hoti ton hēlion autou anatellei epi ponērous kai agathous kai brechei epi dikaious kai adikous.
verses.notes: DIVINE-IMPARTIALITY GROUND. The sun-and-rain-on-good-and-evil topos is widely attested in ancient ethics: Seneca *De Beneficiis* 4.26.1; cf. Stoic *philanthrōpia*. Becoming *huioi* (sons) by imitating the Father's impartial generosity = the principle of *imitatio Dei* (cf. Lev 19:2). **LENS-RISK FLAG**: 'sun and rain' should NOT be pre-resolved into Sitchin/Anunnaki-engineered-meteorology readings; the verse expresses divine impartiality, full stop.

verses.text: ἐὰν γὰρ ἀγαπήσητε τοὺς ἀγαπῶντας ὑμᾶς, τίνα μισθὸν ἔχετε; οὐχὶ καὶ οἱ τελῶναι τὸ αὐτὸ ποιοῦσιν;
verses.translit: ean gar agapēsēte tous agapōntas hymas, tina misthon echete? ouchi kai hoi telōnai to auto poiousin?
verses.notes: The tax-collector example — *telōnai* were despised as Roman-collaborator publicans (cf. Mt 9:10-13; 11:19; 21:31-32). The rhetorical question shows that reciprocal love is morally trivial.

verses.text: καὶ ἐὰν ἀσπάσησθε τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς ὑμῶν μόνον, τί περισσὸν ποιεῖτε; οὐχὶ καὶ οἱ ἐθνικοὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ποιοῦσιν;
verses.translit: kai ean aspasēsthe tous adelphous hymōn monon, ti perisson poieite? ouchi kai hoi ethnikoi to auto poiousin?
verses.notes: *ethnikoi* — Gentiles / pagans, in distinction to Jews. Matthew's use of *ethnikoi* (cf. 6:7; 18:17) is typically pejorative — a Jewish-Christian community marker preserved despite the Gospel's broader universalizing trajectory (cf. 28:19).

verses.text: Ἔσεσθε οὖν ὑμεῖς τέλειοι ὡς ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος τέλειός ἐστιν.
verses.translit: Esesthe oun hymeis teleioi hōs ho patēr hymōn ho ouranios teleios estin.
verses.notes: CONCLUDING CALL TO PERFECTION. *teleios* — 'complete' / 'mature' / 'perfect.' In LXX, *teleios* translates Hebrew *tāmîm* (whole-hearted, unblemished; cf. Gen 6:9 of Noah). The Lukan parallel (Luke 6:36) reads *oiktirmones* (merciful) — possibly the more original Q-form. *patēr ouranios* (heavenly Father) — uniquely Matthean idiom (5:48; 6:14, 26, 32; 15:13; 18:35; 23:9). cf. Davies-Allison ICC 1.561-563.
